extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent practitioners (U.S. and foreign) seeking to use the Patent Prosecution Highway
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for filing a Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) request (including PPH eXtra) to obtain expedited examination of corresponding claims in a later-examining Office (OLE) based on an allowable determination from an earlier-examining Office (OEE).

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH basic principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows applicants who received a determination of allowable claims in an application from one Intellectual Property (IP) Office to obtain fast track processing of corresponding claims in an application pending in other IP Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective strategy for U.S. applicants to get IP rights faster in global markets; participating Offices leverage each other's work to expedite examination when corresponding claims exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable OEE positive examination results
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant receives a positive examination result from a PPH participating Office – Office of earlier examination (OEE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable OEE work product includes a national/regional office action indicating allowability or a PCT Written Opinion or PCT International Preliminary Report on Patentability (where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a PPH request in OLE
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant files a PPH request in a corresponding application in another PPH participating Office – Office of later examination (OLE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the PPH request is granted, the examination of the application in the OLE is expedited. Correspondence between OEE and OLE claim sets must be demonstrated (see 'Corresponding claims' requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH petition form (no fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: A PPH petition form is required to request PPH treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no fee for the PPH petition form at the USPTO; applicants must ensure the petition form is completed according to Office instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required documents for PPH request
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain documents must be submitted with the PPH request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required documents include: a copy of the most recent office action prior to the decision to grant a patent or the most recent PCT work product (translation as necessary), copies of all cited documents, and any Office-specific documents. Provide translations where required by the OLE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding claims requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All the claims must sufficiently correspond to the patentable/allowable claims in the OEE application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OXE-allowable claim set should be leveraged to improve consistency across jurisdictions; applicants must show how claims in the OLE correspond (are commensurate) to the allowed claims in the OEE. Insufficient correspondence may render the PPH request ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution at OLE must not have begun
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH eligibility requires that prosecution at the Office of Later Examination has not begun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If substantive examination or other prosecution has already begun at the OLE, the PPH request will not be appropriate; file PPH before first substantive action at the OLE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of PPH agreements / participating regimes
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH operates under different agreement types: Global PPH, IP5 PPH, and bilateral agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global PPH (began 2014) includes a broad set of participating Offices; IP5 PPH involves the five largest offices (EPO, JPO, KIPO, CNIPA, USPTO); USPTO also maintains multiple bilateral PPH agreements. Eligibility and specific document/claim correspondence rules may vary by agreement and Office—confirm Office-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH eXtra pendency targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary PPH improvement initiative (PPH eXtra) sets pendency timing targets to improve consistency and predictability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendency targets: completion of PPH request to first office action (FA) within 3 months; applicant FA response to subsequent office action within 3 months. These targets aim to make timing more predictable for applicants and to promote timeliness across Offices; participation in PPH eXtra is voluntary and Office-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH performance and efficiency metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures used to evaluate PPH impacts at the USPTO and globally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported metrics include: First Action Allowance Rate, Overall Allowance Rate (includes RCEs), Percent of Applications with at least one RCE, Percent with at least one continuation, First Action Office Mail (FAOM) Pendency (months), Disposal Pendency (months), and Actions per Disposal. These metrics demonstrate that PPH cases often have higher allowance rates and different pendency/efficiency characteristics compared to non-PPH cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of USPTO work product for PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO work products (as OEE) are frequently used by applicants to support PPH requests worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. work product is commonly cited in PPH filings and can help U.S. applicants obtain faster IP rights abroad. Applicants should include the USPTO office action or PCT work product as required when relying on USPTO as the OEE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated Patent Grant (APG) program criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: APG allows an applicant who receives a U.S. patent to request a partner Office to grant a corresponding national application on the basis of the issued U.S. patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant under APG is subject to relevant national laws in the partner country—for example, subject matter eligibility may differ by jurisdiction. Confirm each partner Office's APG requirements and limitations before requesting APG treatment.
